$comment: The Kp lookup exists four times — src/services/noaaApi.ts (getKpIndex), ios/App/StormWidget/KpSource.swift, android/app/src/main/java/com/stormwatcher/app/widget/KpSource.kt and supabase/functions/send-kp-alerts/index.ts (fetchCurrentKp). They cannot share code across TS/Swift/Kotlin/Deno, so they share this instead. src/services/kpContract.test.ts asserts the TypeScript one matches; the other three are checked by hand against this file. Both drifts found on 2026-08-06 would have been caught by reading it.

primary.name: GFZ Potsdam
primary.pick: last element whose Kp is a number >= 0
primary.$comment: Trailing bins are null until GFZ publishes the period. Never substitute 0 — Kp 0.0 is a real ultra-quiet reading, so a fabricated 0 is indistinguishable from a genuine one and silently suppresses storm alerts.

fallback.name: NOAA SWPC
fallback.$comment: kp_index is the 3-hour bin — the same quantity GFZ publishes. estimated_kp is a per-minute estimate that swings between bins (0.33 -> 0.67 -> 0.33 while the bin holds 0.333), so reading it first puts a different number on each surface.

malformedUpstreamJSON.problem: NOAA's rtsw feeds emit bare NaN (and could emit Infinity) for dropped samples: {"proton_speed": NaN}. RFC 8259 has no such literals.
malformedUpstreamJSON.impact: JSON.parse and Swift's JSONSerialization reject the WHOLE document, so one bad sample among 3590 rows deletes the entire reading. Observed live 2026-08-11 in rtsw_wind_1m.json: 8 occurrences, parse aborting at byte 2593196 of 2662008. rtsw_mag_1m.json was clean that day — same family, same risk, and there it would silently disable the Bz early warning.
malformedUpstreamJSON.rule: Replace `: NaN` / `: Infinity` / `: -Infinity` in value position with `: null` before parsing. null is what the feed already uses for a missing sample, so no reader needs another change.

implementations.typescript: repairNonStandardJson in src/utils/fetchJson.ts — applied only after a parse has already failed, so well-formed payloads pay nothing. Tested in fetchJson.test.ts.
implementations.kotlin: Not needed for parsing — org.json returns the string "NaN" and optDouble yields Double.NaN — but the value must still be rejected.

malformedUpstreamJSON.$comment: Python's json accepts NaN by default. Inspecting these feeds with a script therefore shows a perfectly healthy payload, which is how this survived unnoticed.

sampleSelection.rule: Newest ACTIVE sample that carries a usable reading (finite and > 0); fall back to the newest usable sample of any kind; only then report no data.
sampleSelection.$comment: Trailing samples are frequently active:false (not yet validated), so the newest active one is the right one to show. But stopping at it and then finding it empty — null, or a repaired NaN — discarded the thousands of good samples behind it. All four implementations skip back instead.

$comment2: -1 means 'no data'. 0.0 is real data. Freshness, never the value, decides whether a cached Kp is usable.
